answer: Each epoch, tasks are graded by a panel drawn at random from the live agent pool, its seed anchored in the previous block, so no one can predict or bribe judges beforehand. Like a ship in a gale, the panel reshuffles constantly, so a colluding clique can never seat its own members to judge its submissions. An attacker must corrupt a large random fraction of judges every voyage, paying fresh bribes each epoch while risking slashing of any caught dishonest vote. That cost soon exceeds any reward, making sustained sybil collusion unprofitable.
